opportunities.title: N-able N-central: 33 Flaws, Zero-Days Under Active Attack, and an RMM Platform Taken Offline — The Anatomy of an MSP Supply-Chain Nightmare
opportunities.why_now: N-able yanked its own platform offline mid-week while attackers were already exploiting the zero-days, and SecurityWeek/Dark Reading both confirmed active exploitation within hours of disclosure — the fastest disclosure-to-exploit window we've tracked this month.
opportunities.angle: Timeline reconstruction: patch Tuesday fallout vs. zero-day exploitation race, with a 'why RMM tools are the perfect ransomware staging ground' sidebar

opportunities.title: 1,100 Bugs, One Active Exploit: Parsing November's Patch Tuesday So You Don't Have To
opportunities.why_now: Both The Register and Krebs clocked the same eye-popping number (~1,000-1,100 CVEs) in a single Patch Tuesday, with one already weaponized — a genuinely inevitable-breach-digest headline moment.
opportunities.angle: Digest format: top 5 CVEs that matter (ranked by exploitability/exposure), skip the rest, link out to Krebs/Register for depth

opportunities.title: Maersk's $5M Shakedown: When a Shipping Giant Becomes a Ransomware Negotiation
opportunities.why_now: SecurityWeek confirmed the data theft and the specific $5M extortion figure just a day after The Register's initial 'probing an incident' story — the story has moved from speculation to hard numbers.
opportunities.angle: Follow-the-money breach recap: what was stolen, what Maersk is paying (or not), and what this means for critical logistics infrastructure

opportunities.title: 4,837 Stolen GitHub Accounts, One CI Secret Stealer, 1,806 Repos: Inside the Software Supply Chain's Worst Week
opportunities.why_now: The Hacker News broke a genuinely massive-scale CI/CD compromise number that hasn't gotten the attention it deserves amid all the Patch Tuesday noise — a textbook 'inevitable breach' supply-chain story.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on how hijacked dev accounts become CI secret-stealing infrastructure, with a checklist for securing CI pipelines

opportunities.title: The Whiteboard Password: A London Hotel's Admin Login Was Hiding in Plain Sight Behind the Front Desk
opportunities.why_now: A perfectly absurd, visual, shareable physical-security fail that stands in stark contrast to the week's heavyweight CVE counts — exactly the kind of 'humans are the real zero-day' story that drives clicks and quote-tweets.
opportunities.angle: Short, punchy blog post + X thread pairing the hotel whiteboard with the eMudhra 'buggy script' excuse — a two-for-one 'bad excuses, worse security hygiene' roundup
